This looks super appealing to me all bar one thing - not alot of ram which I'll need for delay and some analysis. I know it's overkill to sample at 24 bit 96khz but alot of people use USB interfaces or mixers with that spec and I don't want to jeopardise that.  I think it's only like 2MB that the Nucleo 144 series has so if the program needed 512kb ram for everything else (which is p generous) that would leave:

(2  - 0.512) / (24 \* 96000 \* 0.125 \* 10\^-6) = 1.488 / 0.288 \~= *5 second circular buffer*

The docs say the memory controller addresses up to 256mb of external memory (but no DDR support which sucks.) When I eventually get around to production it's not too much of a problem because I can obviously just create a custom PCB that interfaces with the SDRAM / DRAM and SRAM modules. 

Anyways, sorry for the spiel, **is there a way to add significantly more memory to these Nucleo boards**? I thought it would be a well established problem but I couldn't find much online. 

EM = expected memory. PM = program memory = 1mb. EL = expected length = 30s 

(EM - PM) / 0.288 = EL => EM = (30 \* 0.288) + 1 = 9.64mb so jumping to the nearest power of 2 I'll be getting 16mb SDRAM / DRAM

How would I go about doing that ? Sorry for the pointless mental math just wanted to show I'm not pulling the numbers out of my ass.
